report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of envelope.py: adopt_trace, stamp, subject_for, statement, is_statement, and constants. All docstring claims are checkable within this chunk except those referencing external functions or behaviors.

handoff.purpose: Define trace adoption, stamping, in-toto statement helpers, and subject creation.

symbols.name: adopt_trace
symbols.note: Context manager that continues a trace from an external trace_id; never mints.

symbols.name: stamp
symbols.note: Returns a copy of record with trace_id if present; preserves existing trace_id.

symbols.name: IN_TOTO_STATEMENT_TYPE
symbols.note: String constant for in-toto Statement v1 type URI.

symbols.name: _PREDICATE_BASE
symbols.note: Base URI for local predicate types, using .invalid domain.

symbols.name: subject_for
symbols.note: Creates a subject dict with name and sha256 digest.

symbols.name: statement
symbols.note: Wraps payload into ITE-6 statement shape with subject, predicate_type, predicate, and optional trace_id.

symbols.name: is_statement
symbols.note: Checks if an object is an in-toto statement by _type and predicate presence.

claims.text: CONTINUE a run someone else started. **Never mints.**
claims.why: The function calls _scope with the given trace_id; whether it mints depends on _scope implementation not in this chunk.

claims.text: It binds exactly what it was handed, and binds ``None`` when it was handed nothing.
claims.why: The function passes trace_id directly to _scope; if trace_id is None, _scope receives None.

claims.text: A COPY of ``record`` carrying the trace id, or unchanged when there is none.
claims.why: Function creates a new dict from record and adds trace_id only if one exists.

claims.text: Additive and non-destructive by contract: the caller's dict is never mutated
claims.why: Function creates a new dict via dict(record or {}), leaving original unchanged.

claims.text: an existing ``trace_id`` already on the record WINS over the ambient one
claims.why: Function returns early if out.get(TRACE_KEY) is truthy, before checking ambient trace_id.

claims.text: Pass ``sha256`` when the digest ALREADY EXISTS -- the spine ledger stores ``payload_sha`` in the row, and recomputing it here would silently paper over the one disagreement worth surfacing
claims.why: Refers to spine ledger behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Pass ``payload`` only when no digest has been computed yet; it is hashed through :func:`canonical_json`, so the digest does not depend on dict insertion order.
claims.why: Refers to canonical_sha function not defined in this chunk.
Function places predicate as-is under 'predicate' key without modification.

claims.text: ``predicate`` is placed under the ``predicate`` key exactly as given -- no key is added to it, removed from it or renamed inside it.
claims.why: Function assigns predicate directly to out['predicate'].

claims.text: ``subject`` accepts one subject or a list; in-toto's field is a list and it is normalised to one here so callers do not each remember to wrap.
claims.why: Function converts single subject to a list via list(subject) or wraps in list.

claims.text: Tested on ``_type`` plus the presence of ``predicate``, not on ``_type`` alone: a legacy payload that happens to carry a ``_type`` string must not be mistaken for a statement and unwrapped down to nothing.
claims.why: Function checks both _type equality and existence of 'predicate' key.

observations.what: adopt_trace docstring claims 'Never mints' but minting logic is in _scope, not visible here.
subject_for docstring references canonical_sha and canonical_json; these are not defined in this chunk.
stamp function uses TRACE_KEY constant which is not defined in this chunk; likely imported from elsewhere.
statement function uses current_trace_id() and TRACE_KEY; these are not defined in this chunk.
is_statement returns a bool; docstring says 'Is this an envelope, or a bare pre-envelope record?' but function only checks _type and predicate, not envelope-specific fields.
